output.summary: A rainforest herb native to eastern Australia, cunjevoi has very large, glossy, spade-shaped leaves and heavily scented greenish-cream flowers. The plant is poisonous: eating any part causes immediate pain, burning and swelling of the lips, tongue and mouth, and its sap can irritate skin and eyes.
output.edibilityNote: All parts are poisonous when eaten, causing immediate oral pain, burning and swelling; a small number of children have died.
